question: What is the most powerful weapon that enables the Parliament to ensure executive accountability?
solution_text:
The correct answer is The no-confidence motion.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "no-confidence motion" is the most powerful weapon available to Parliament for enforcing executive accountability. If a no-confidence motion is passed by a majority in the Lok Sabha, the entire Council of Ministers must resign. (अविश्वास प्रस्ताव)

• It flows from Article 75(3) of the Constitution, which lays down that the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• A no-confidence motion can be moved only in the Lok Sabha, and it needs the support of at least 50 members to be admitted.

• Other parliamentary devices of control are comparatively weaker: Question Hour, Zero Hour, adjournment motion, calling attention motion, censure motion, cut motions and the committee system.

• A censure motion differs from a no-confidence motion — it states reasons, may be moved against an individual minister, and its passage does not compel the government to resign.

NOTE

• India's first no-confidence motion was moved by Acharya J. B. Kripalani in 1963 against the Nehru government.

• The government of Morarji Desai (1979) and V. P. Singh (1990) fell after facing such motions; Atal Bihari Vajpayee's government lost a confidence vote by one vote in 1999.

question: Where is the Mahabodhi temple situated?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bodh Gaya.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Mahabodhi Temple" is situated at Bodh Gaya in the Gaya district of Bihar. It marks the spot where Gautama Buddha attained enlightenment (bodhi) under the Bodhi tree (a peepal tree). (महाबोधि मंदिर — बोधगया, बिहार)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The temple was originally built by Emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE; the present brick structure dates largely from the 5th–6th century CE (Gupta period).

• It was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2002 and is one of the earliest surviving brick temples in India.

• The Mahabodhi Temple Act, 1949 governs its management.

NOTE

• The four principal Buddhist pilgrimage sites: Lumbini (birth, Nepal), Bodh Gaya (enlightenment, Bihar), Sarnath (first sermon, near Varanasi, UP) and Kushinagar (mahaparinirvana, UP).

• Other Buddhist sites in Bihar: Nalanda, Vikramshila, Rajgir (Griddhakuta hill) and Vaishali.

question: Which African leader wrote the autobiography ‘ Long Walk to Freedom’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nelson Mandela.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Long Walk to Freedom" (published in 1994) is the autobiography of Nelson Mandela, the anti-apartheid revolutionary who became the first black President of South Africa (1994–1999). (नेल्सन मंडेला — लॉन्ग वॉक टू फ्रीडम)

• Much of the book was written secretly during his 27 years of imprisonment, largely on Robben Island.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Nelson Mandela was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1993 (jointly with F. W. de Klerk) and India's highest civilian honour, the Bharat Ratna, in 1990 — he was only the second foreigner to receive it after Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan.

• He was affectionately called "Madiba"; his birthday, 18 July, is observed as Nelson Mandela International Day by the UN.

• He was often described as the "Gandhi of South Africa" for his commitment to non-violent struggle.

NOTE

• Other options: Robert Mugabe (Zimbabwe), Muammar Gaddafi (Libya) and Archbishop Desmond Tutu (South Africa, Nobel Peace Prize 1984, chaired the Truth and Reconciliation Commission).

question: In which year was the Training of Rural Youth for Self Employment (TRYSEM) scheme launched by Government of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1979.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Training of Rural Youth for Self Employment (TRYSEM)" scheme was launched by the Government of India in 1979 (on 15 August 1979). (ट्राइसेम — 1979)

• Its objective was to provide technical skills and training to rural youth (aged 18–35) from below-poverty-line families so that they could take up self-employment in agriculture, industry, services and business.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• TRYSEM operated as a sub-component of the Integrated Rural Development Programme (IRDP), which itself was launched in 1978–80.

• In 1999, TRYSEM was merged, along with IRDP, DWCRA, SITRA, GKY and MWS, into the single self-employment programme "Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY)".

• SGSY was later restructured as the National Rural Livelihoods Mission (NRLM) / Aajeevika (2011), and skill training for rural youth now runs under DDU-GKY (2014).

NOTE

• Landmark rural development schemes for SSC: CDP (1952), IRDP (1978), TRYSEM (1979), JRY (1989), EAS (1993), PMGSY (2000), SGSY (1999), NREGA/MGNREGA (2005/2006), NRLM (2011), DDU-GKY (2014).

question: Under the Chief Minister Learn and Earn Scheme of Madhya Pradesh, the government will NOT provide which of the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Laptops.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Mukhyamantri Seekho–Kamao Yojana (Chief Minister Learn and Earn Scheme)" of Madhya Pradesh, launched in 2023, provides on-the-job training, employable skills and a monthly stipend (financial assistance) to educated unemployed youth. (मुख्यमंत्री सीखो-कमाओ योजना)

• The scheme does NOT provide laptops — laptop distribution is a separate state initiative for meritorious students.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Eligibility: youth of Madhya Pradesh aged 18–29 years, who have passed Class 12 / ITI / diploma / graduation or higher.

• Trainees receive a monthly stipend of roughly ₹8,000–₹10,000, of which 75% is paid by the state government and the rest by the establishment.

• Training is offered in about 700+ work areas, and trainees also get a certificate from the MP State Skill Development Board.

NOTE

• Comparable skilling schemes: PMKVY (Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana, 2015), DDU-GKY (2014) for rural youth, and the National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS).

question: Noted dance historian Dr. Sunil Kothari was awarded Madhabdev Award in 2019 by the Government of Assam for popularising which dance form of the state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sattriya.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Dr. Sunil Kothari, the noted dance historian, scholar and critic, was conferred the "Madhabdev Award" in 2019 by the Government of Assam for his outstanding contribution to popularising the Sattriya dance form of the state. (सत्रीय नृत्य — असम)

• Sattriya was introduced in the 15th century by the great Vaishnava saint-reformer Srimanta Sankardeva as a medium of devotional expression in the monasteries (sattras) of Assam.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Sattriya was formally recognised as a classical dance form by the Sangeet Natak Akademi in 2000, becoming the eighth Indian classical dance.

• The Madhabdev Award is named after Madhavdeva, the chief disciple of Srimanta Sankardeva.

• Dr. Sunil Kothari was honoured with the Padma Shri (2001) and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (1995).

NOTE

• The eight classical dances of India: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (Uttar Pradesh), Kathakali and Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur) and Sattriya (Assam).

• The other options are folk forms: Bihu (Assam's harvest dance), Bagurumba (Bodo tribe of Assam) and Ojapali (a narrative song-and-dance tradition of Assam).

question: What is the usual term used to describe the climate of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tropical monsoon.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The climate of India is usually described as the "tropical monsoon" type (in Koppen's scheme, "Amw" – tropical monsoon climate). The word "monsoon" comes from the Arabic "mausim", meaning season, and refers to the seasonal reversal of wind direction. (उष्णकटिबंधीय मानसूनी जलवायु)

• The Tropic of Cancer (23½°N) passes through the middle of the country, so India lies partly in the tropical and partly in the sub-tropical zone, but the overall character is monsoonal.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The four seasons recognised by the India Meteorological Department (IMD):

◦ Winter (December–February), Summer/Pre-monsoon (March–May), South-West Monsoon / rainy season (June–September) and Post-monsoon / retreating monsoon (October–November).

• The South-West monsoon gives India about 75% of its annual rainfall; it normally reaches Kerala around 1 June and withdraws by mid-September.

• Mawsynram and Cherrapunji (Sohra) in Meghalaya are among the wettest places on Earth, while Jaisalmer (Rajasthan) is among the driest.

NOTE

• The Himalayas act as a climatic divide, blocking the cold Central Asian winds, and the Western Ghats cause heavy orographic rainfall on their windward side with a rain-shadow area to their east.

question: Dandari (Dancing) troupes perform __________ during the festival of Diwali for a fortnight with participation from Kolam and Raj Gond tribes.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ghusadi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Ghusadi (Gusadi)" is the celebrated tribal dance performed by Dandari troupes during the Diwali festival for a fortnight, with participation from the Kolam and Raj Gond tribes. (घुसडी नृत्य)

• It is popular in the Adilabad district of Telangana and the adjoining Gond areas of Maharashtra. Male dancers wear headgear of peacock feathers, animal-skin garments, beards of goat hair and smear ash on their bodies.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Kanaka Raju, a Gond tribal artist from Adilabad, was awarded the Padma Shri in 2021 for popularising the Gusadi dance.

• The Gonds are among the largest tribal groups in India, spread across Telangana, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra and Odisha.

NOTE

• The other options are also folk/tribal dances: Chhau (a masked martial dance of Odisha, Jharkhand and West Bengal — inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2010), Baiga Pardhoni (a wedding dance of the Baiga tribe of Madhya Pradesh) and Rout Nacha (a cowherd community dance of Chhattisgarh performed at Diwali).

question: How many gold medals did India win at the ISSF Junior World Cup 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 6.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India won 6 gold medals at the ISSF Junior World Cup 2023, finishing on top of the medal tally. (आईएसएसएफ जूनियर विश्व कप 2023 — भारत को 6 स्वर्ण)

• The ISSF (International Shooting Sport Federation) Junior World Cup is the premier global shooting competition for junior athletes, held in rifle, pistol and shotgun events.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The ISSF was founded in 1907 and has its headquarters at Munich, Germany.

• India has emerged as a shooting powerhouse at the junior level, regularly topping ISSF Junior World Championship and Junior World Cup medal tables.

• The National Rifle Association of India (NRAI), founded in 1951, is the governing body for shooting sport in India.

NOTE

• Indian shooting greats: Abhinav Bindra (India's first individual Olympic gold, 10 m air rifle, Beijing 2008), Rajyavardhan Singh Rathore (silver, Athens 2004), Gagan Narang, Vijay Kumar, Manu Bhaker and Saurabh Chaudhary.

question: _____________ is the first Indian woman to have won a Grammy.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tanvi Shah.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Tanvi Shah is the first Indian woman to win a Grammy Award. She won it in 2010 for the song "Jai Ho" from the film *Slumdog Millionaire*, in the category Best Song Written for Motion Picture, Television or Other Visual Media. (तन्वी शाह — ग्रैमी जीतने वाली पहली भारतीय महिला)

• She wrote and sang the Spanish portions of the song, and shared the award with A. R. Rahman and lyricist Gulzar.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• At the 52nd Grammy Awards (2010), A. R. Rahman won two Grammys — Best Compilation Soundtrack Album and Best Song Written for Visual Media — for *Slumdog Millionaire*.

• Other Indian Grammy winners include Pandit Ravi Shankar (the first Indian, 1968), Zakir Hussain, Vishwa Mohan Bhatt, Ricky Kej and Falguni Shah (Falu).

NOTE

• The Grammy Awards are presented annually by the Recording Academy of the United States for outstanding achievement in the music industry; they began in 1959.

• The other options — Shalmali Kholgade, Palak Muchhal and Shilpa Rao — are well-known Indian playback singers but have not won a Grammy.

question: Which Indian musician personality’s native place is West Bengal?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bappi Lahiri.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Bappi Lahiri (born Alokesh Lahiri, 1952–2022) hailed from Jalpaiguri in West Bengal. He was a celebrated music director, singer and composer who introduced disco music to Indian cinema. (बप्पी लहरी — पश्चिम बंगाल)

• He is remembered for chart-busting scores in films such as *Disco Dancer*, *Namak Halaal*, *Sharaabi*, *Himmatwala* and *Dance Dance*, and for his trademark gold jewellery.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Naushad Ali (1919–2006) was from Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh; he composed for *Baiju Bawra*, *Mughal-e-Azam* and received the Dadasaheb Phalke Award (1981).

• O. P. Nayyar (1926–2007) was born in Lahore (undivided Punjab) and was famous for never using Lata Mangeshkar's voice.

• Ilaiyaraaja (born 1943) is from Tamil Nadu; he is a Padma Vibhushan awardee and was nominated to the Rajya Sabha.

NOTE

• Famous musicians from West Bengal: Rabindranath Tagore, Salil Chowdhury, S. D. Burman (born in Comilla, of the Tripura royal family, but long associated with Bengal), R. D. Burman, Hemanta Mukherjee, Manna Dey and Pandit Ravi Shankar.

question: According to the Census of India 2011, which State/Union Territory has the lowest sex ratio?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Daman and Diu.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the Census of India 2011, the Union Territory of Daman and Diu recorded the lowest sex ratio among all States/UTs, at only 618 females per 1,000 males. (दमन और दीव — 618)

• The extremely low figure is explained mainly by heavy in-migration of male industrial workers into the UT's factories.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Sex ratio in India (2011) = 943 females per 1,000 males (up from 933 in 2001).

• Kerala has the highest sex ratio (1,084), followed by Puducherry (1,037); among UTs the lowest after Daman and Diu are Dadra and Nagar Haveli (774) and Chandigarh (818).

• Among states, Haryana has the lowest sex ratio (879), followed by Jammu and Kashmir (889).

• The child sex ratio (0–6 years) in 2011 was 919, the lowest since Independence.

NOTE

• Census 2011 was the 15th national census and the 7th since Independence. Its motto was "Our Census, Our Future".

• Other Census 2011 facts: literacy rate 74.04% (Kerala highest at 93.91%, Bihar lowest at 61.80%); most populous state — Uttar Pradesh; least populous — Sikkim; highest density — Bihar (1,106/km²).

question: Which of the following is an autobiography of the famous cricketer Sourav Ganguly?
option_4: Memories of My Life and Times
solution_text:
The correct answer is A Century is not enough.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "A Century Is Not Enough" (2018), co-written with Gautam Bhattacharya, is the autobiography of the former Indian cricket captain Sourav Ganguly. (सौरव गांगुली की आत्मकथा)

• Nicknamed "Dada" and the "Prince of Kolkata", Ganguly captained India from 2000 to 2005 and is credited with rebuilding the team after the match-fixing crisis.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Sourav Ganguly served as President of the BCCI (2019–2022) and earlier as President of the Cricket Association of Bengal.

• He scored 131 on Test debut at Lord's (1996) and was one of the finest ODI batsmen of his generation, with over 11,000 ODI runs.

NOTE

• Matching the other titles: "A Shot at History" — Abhinav Bindra; "The Dream of Revolution" — a biography of Jayaprakash Narayan (by Bimal Prasad and Sujata Prasad); "Memories of My Life and Times" — Bipin Chandra Pal.

• Other cricket autobiographies: "Playing It My Way" (Sachin Tendulkar), "The Test of My Life" (Yuvraj Singh), "Straight from the Heart" (Kapil Dev), "Sunny Days" (Sunil Gavaskar).

question:
Consider the following statement about the Government of India Act, 1935.

1. This act was enacted by the British Parliament.

2. This Act was divided into two separate acts for India and Burma Government.

3. This act was commenced from the 1 April 1935.

Select the correct statement(s) using the code given below.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both 1 and 2.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Statement 1 is CORRECT — the Government of India Act, 1935 was passed/enacted by the British Parliament in August 1935. It was the longest Act ever enacted by the British Parliament up to that time (321 sections and 10 schedules). (भारत शासन अधिनियम, 1935)

• Statement 2 is CORRECT — the Act was later split into two separate Acts, namely the Government of India Act, 1935 and the Government of Burma Act, 1935, since Burma was separated from India in 1937.

• Statement 3 is INCORRECT — the Act did not commence on 1 April 1935. Its provincial provisions came into force on 1 April 1937, when provincial autonomy was introduced and elections were held in 1937.

• Hence only statements 1 and 2 are correct.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Main features of the GoI Act, 1935:

◦ Provided for an All-India Federation of provinces and princely states (this part never came into being).

◦ Abolished dyarchy in the provinces and introduced provincial autonomy; introduced dyarchy at the Centre.

◦ Divided powers into three lists — Federal, Provincial and Concurrent — with residuary powers given to the Viceroy.

◦ Provided for a Federal Court (established 1937) and the Reserve Bank of India (1935).

◦ Extended separate electorates to depressed classes, women and labour.

NOTE

• The GoI Act, 1935 is often called the "blueprint of the Indian Constitution" — a large part of the Constitution of India (federal scheme, office of Governor, emergency provisions, public service commissions) is derived from it.

question: Who among the following established a unit of horsepower that is equal to one horse doing 33,000 foot - pounds of work in one minute?
solution_text:
The correct answer is James Watt.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Scottish inventor and engineer James Watt (1736–1819) defined the unit "horsepower" as the work done by one horse equal to 33,000 foot-pounds of work per minute. (जेम्स वाट — अश्वशक्ति)

• He devised the unit to help market his improved steam engine by comparing its output with the draught horses it replaced.

• 1 horsepower (mechanical) = 33,000 ft·lb/min = 550 ft·lb/s ≈ 746 watts.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The SI unit of power, the "watt (W)", is named in his honour. 1 watt = 1 joule per second.

• Watt's key contribution was the separate condenser (1765), which vastly improved the efficiency of the Newcomen steam engine and became a driving force of the Industrial Revolution.

NOTE

• Other "James" scientists in the options: James Croll (theory of ice ages and orbital forcing), James Dwight Dana (American geologist and mineralogist, author of *System of Mineralogy*), and Joseph Black (Scottish chemist known for latent heat, often confused with "James Black").

• Units named after scientists: newton (force), joule (energy), pascal (pressure), hertz (frequency), ampere (current), volt (potential difference), ohm (resistance).

question: In which year was the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act passed?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1976.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act was passed in 1976, during the National Emergency (1975–77) under the government of Indira Gandhi. (42वाँ संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम — 1976)

• It is the most comprehensive amendment ever made and is popularly called the "Mini-Constitution" or the "Constitution of Indira".

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Major changes made by the 42nd Amendment:

◦ Added the words "SOCIALIST", "SECULAR" and "INTEGRITY" to the Preamble.

◦ Added Part IV-A — Fundamental Duties (Article 51A), on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee.

◦ Added Article 39A (free legal aid), 43A (workers' participation) and 48A (protection of environment) to the Directive Principles.

◦ Transferred five subjects from the State List to the Concurrent List — education, forests, weights and measures, protection of wild animals and birds, and administration of justice.

◦ Made the President bound by the advice of the Council of Ministers and extended the term of the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies from 5 to 6 years.

NOTE

• The 44th Amendment Act, 1978 (Janata Party government) reversed many of these changes — it restored the 5-year term, removed the Right to Property from Fundamental Rights (making it a legal right under Article 300A) and replaced "internal disturbance" with "armed rebellion" as a ground for National Emergency.

question: Who among the following leaders led the Revolt of 1857 in Bihar?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kunwar Singh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Babu Kunwar Singh (Veer Kunwar Singh), the zamindar of Jagdishpur in Shahabad (present-day Bhojpur district), Bihar, led the Revolt of 1857 in Bihar. (वीर कुंवर सिंह — बिहार, 1857)

• He was about 80 years old at the time of the revolt and is remembered for his brilliant guerrilla tactics against the British. He died in April 1858, shortly after a famous victory near Jagdishpur.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Leaders of the Revolt of 1857 at various centres:

◦ Delhi — Bahadur Shah Zafar / General Bakht Khan

◦ Kanpur — Nana Sahib and Tantia Tope

◦ Lucknow — Begum Hazrat Mahal

◦ Jhansi — Rani Lakshmibai

◦ Bareilly — Khan Bahadur Khan

◦ Faizabad — Maulvi Ahmadullah Shah

• The revolt began at Meerut on 10 May 1857, sparked by the greased cartridges of the Enfield rifle; Mangal Pandey of the 34th Native Infantry had already revolted at Barrackpore on 29 March 1857.

NOTE

• The other options belong to a much later period: Dr. Rajendra Prasad (first President of India) and Rajkumar Shukla (who persuaded Gandhiji to visit Champaran in 1917) were both from Bihar but of the 20th century.

• The revolt led to the Government of India Act, 1858, which ended Company rule and transferred power to the British Crown.

question: Shri Jagannathji Mela is held at _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Alwar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Shri Jagannathji Mela" is a well-known fair held at Alwar in Rajasthan. (श्री जगन्नाथजी मेला — अलवर, राजस्थान)

• It is celebrated with a grand rath yatra (chariot procession) of Lord Jagannath in the month of Ashadha (June–July) and attracts large crowds from the surrounding districts.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Alwar is part of Rajasthan's Mewat region and is famous for the Bala Qila (Alwar Fort), the City Palace, Siliserh Lake and the Sariska Tiger Reserve.

• Other important fairs of Rajasthan: Pushkar Fair (Ajmer — camel fair, Kartik Purnima), Urs of Khwaja Muinuddin Chishti (Ajmer), Teej Fair (Jaipur), Gangaur (Jaipur), Nagaur Cattle Fair, Baneshwar Fair (Dungarpur, the "tribal Kumbh") and Kolayat Fair (Bikaner).

NOTE

• The world-famous Jagannath Rath Yatra of Puri, Odisha, is a different, much larger festival; Cuttack and Sambalpur (Odisha) are known respectively for the Bali Yatra and the Sitalsasthi Carnival.

question: _____________ literally means 'dance of the enchantress'. It is one of the most striking in the Indian classical dance repertoire.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mohiniyattam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Mohiniyattam" literally means the "dance of the enchantress" — from "Mohini", the enchanting female form taken by Lord Vishnu, and "attam", meaning dance. (मोहिनीअट्टम — केरल)

• It is a classical dance form of Kerala, performed solo by women, marked by gentle, swaying, lasya (graceful/feminine) movements resembling the swaying of palm trees.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Costume: a plain off-white (kasavu) sari with a gold border, with the hair tied in a bun on the left side and adorned with jasmine flowers.

• The dance is based on the Hastalakshanadeepika and follows the Natya Shastra; the accompanying music is in the Sopana style, sung in Manipravalam (a mix of Sanskrit and Malayalam).

• Kalyanikutty Amma is called the "mother of Mohiniyattam" for reviving it; the poet Vallathol Narayana Menon revived it through the Kerala Kalamandalam (1930).

NOTE

• Meanings of other classical dances: Kathakali (Kerala — "story-play", performed by men with elaborate make-up), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh — named after the village Kuchelapuram), Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu — Bha-Ra-Ta = bhava, raga, tala), Odissi (Odisha), Kathak (from "katha" — story), Manipuri and Sattriya.

question: The important milestones of the SHG Bank linkage movement was spearheaded by _______ with support from RBI.
solution_text:
The correct answer is NABARD.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The SHG (Self-Help Group) – Bank Linkage Programme was spearheaded by NABARD (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development) with the support of the Reserve Bank of India. (नाबार्ड — स्वयं सहायता समूह बैंक लिंकेज कार्यक्रम)

• It was launched as a pilot project in 1992 to link 500 SHGs with banks and has grown into the largest microfinance programme in the world in terms of outreach.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• NABARD was established on 12 July 1982 on the recommendation of the B. Sivaraman Committee, with its headquarters at Mumbai.

• Its functions include providing refinance to Regional Rural Banks, cooperative banks and other rural credit institutions, and supervising RRBs and cooperative banks.

• A Self-Help Group is a small voluntary association, usually of 10–20 women from a similar socio-economic background, that pools savings and gives small loans to members.

NOTE

• SEBI (1988/1992) regulates the securities market, not rural credit.

• Related institutions: RBI (central bank, 1935), SIDBI (small industries, 1990), EXIM Bank (1982), NHB (National Housing Bank, 1988).

• The National Rural Livelihoods Mission (NRLM/Aajeevika) also works through SHGs for poverty alleviation.

question: Narendra Modi Cricket Stadium is one of the premier stadiums in India located at __________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ahmedabad.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Narendra Modi Stadium" is located at Motera in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, on the banks of the Sabarmati river. (नरेंद्र मोदी स्टेडियम — अहमदाबाद)

• With a seating capacity of about 1,32,000, it is the largest cricket stadium in the world. It was rebuilt and inaugurated in February 2021, and forms part of the Sardar Patel Sports Enclave.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The stadium hosted the final of the ICC Men's Cricket World Cup 2023 (19 November 2023), in which Australia defeated India to win their sixth title.

• It is managed by the Gujarat Cricket Association and was designed by the Australian firm Populous.

• It also hosted the "Namaste Trump" event in February 2020.

NOTE

• Other major Indian cricket stadiums: Eden Gardens (Kolkata — the oldest, 1864), Wankhede Stadium (Mumbai), Arun Jaitley Stadium (Delhi, formerly Feroz Shah Kotla), M. A. Chidambaram Stadium (Chennai), M. Chinnaswamy Stadium (Bengaluru) and the Rajiv Gandhi International Stadium (Hyderabad).

question: The pre-monsoon showers are known as ________ in Kerala and Karnataka.
solution_text:
The correct answer is mango showers.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The pre-monsoon showers that occur in Kerala and coastal Karnataka during April–May are known as "mango showers", because they help in the early ripening of mangoes. (आम्र वर्षा / मैंगो शावर)

• They are caused by local convectional thunderstorms in the hot summer months before the arrival of the South-West monsoon.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Regional names of local storms and pre-monsoon showers in India:

◦ Blossom shower / Cherry blossom — Karnataka, helps coffee flowers to bloom.

◦ Kalbaisakhi (Nor'westers) — West Bengal, Assam and Bihar; violent evening thunderstorms of Baisakh, also called "Bordoisila" in Assam.

◦ Loo — hot, dry, dust-laden wind of the northern plains in May–June.

◦ Mango shower — Kerala and coastal Karnataka.

NOTE

• Kalbaisakhi showers are beneficial for tea, jute and rice in eastern India.

• The South-West monsoon normally sets in over Kerala around 1 June and covers the whole country by mid-July; its withdrawal begins in September from north-west India.

question: Insufficient levels of parathyroid hormone and low amount of calcium in the blood causes which of the following conditions?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hypocalcemia.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Hypocalcemia" is the condition of an abnormally low level of calcium in the blood. It results when the parathyroid glands secrete insufficient parathyroid hormone (PTH) — a state called hypoparathyroidism. (रक्त में कैल्शियम की कमी)

• PTH is the main regulator of calcium and phosphorus in the body: it raises blood calcium by releasing it from bones, increasing absorption in the intestine and reducing loss through the kidneys.

• Symptoms include muscle cramps, tetany, numbness and tingling (paraesthesia) and, in severe cases, convulsions.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The opposite condition, hypercalcemia (excess calcium), results from hyperparathyroidism and can cause kidney stones and bone weakening.

• The parathyroid glands are four small glands located behind the thyroid gland in the neck.

• Calcitonin, secreted by the thyroid, has the opposite effect to PTH — it lowers blood calcium.

NOTE

• Other endocrine facts for SSC: Pituitary — "master gland"; Thyroxine deficiency causes goitre/cretinism; Insulin deficiency causes diabetes mellitus; Adrenaline is the "emergency/fight-or-flight hormone".

• The other options are unrelated: Malaria is caused by the *Plasmodium* parasite spread by the female *Anopheles* mosquito; Anaemia is a deficiency of haemoglobin/red blood cells (often due to iron deficiency).

question: Team Rest of India won Irani Cup in 2023. Irani Cup was hosted in which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Irani Cup 2023 was hosted in Madhya Pradesh, at the Holkar Stadium, Indore, in March 2023. Rest of India defeated the Ranji Trophy champions Madhya Pradesh to lift the trophy. (ईरानी कप 2023 — मध्य प्रदेश)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Irani Cup (started in 1959–60) is played annually between the Ranji Trophy winning team and a Rest of India side. It is named after Z. R. Irani, a long-serving member of the BCCI.

• Rest of India has won the Irani Cup the maximum number of times.

• Madhya Pradesh had won the Ranji Trophy 2021–22 under captain Aditya Shrivastava and coach Chandrakant Pandit, beating Mumbai in the final.

NOTE

• Major domestic cricket tournaments in India: Ranji Trophy (first-class, since 1934–35), Duleep Trophy (zonal, 1961–62), Irani Cup (1959–60), Vijay Hazare Trophy (one-day), Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy (T20) and the Deodhar Trophy.

question: What is a dimension related to the sustainability of microfinance institutions in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dependency on donor funding.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sustainability of a Microfinance Institution (MFI) means its ability to cover its costs from its own operations and continue functioning in the long run without outside support.

• Therefore, "dependency on donor funding" (grants, subsidies and soft loans from donors) is the key dimension of sustainability — the greater the dependence on donors, the less sustainable the institution, because such funding is uncertain and temporary. (दानदाता निधि पर निर्भरता)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Sustainability of MFIs is usually assessed on two levels:

◦ Operational Self-Sufficiency (OSS) — whether operating income covers operating costs, loan losses and financing costs.

◦ Financial Self-Sufficiency (FSS) — whether income covers all costs after adjusting for subsidies and inflation.

• Other dimensions include outreach (breadth and depth), repayment/recovery rate, operating efficiency and portfolio quality.

NOTE

• Microfinance provides small loans, savings and insurance to low-income households without collateral. The concept was pioneered by Prof. Muhammad Yunus through the Grameen Bank of Bangladesh (Nobel Peace Prize, 2006).

• In India, microfinance operates mainly through the SHG–Bank Linkage model (NABARD) and the MFI (JLG) model; NBFC-MFIs are regulated by the RBI, and the Malegam Committee (2011) framed key recommendations after the Andhra Pradesh microfinance crisis.
